cases.sentence: Между пленными и конвойными произошло ___ и ожидание чего-то счастливого и торжественного.
cases.explain: «радостное смятение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A pleasant feeling of excitement and an expectation of something joyful and solemn was aroused among the soldiers of the convoy and the prisoners. From all sides came shouts of command, and from the left came smartly dressed cavalrymen on good horses, passing the prisoners at a trot. The expression on all faces showed the tension people feel at the approach of those in authority. The prisoners thronged together and were pushed off the road. The convoy formed up.

cases.sentence: Со всех сторон послышались крики команды, и с ___, рысью объезжая пленных, показались кавалеристы хорошо одетые, на хороших лошадях.
cases.explain: «левой стороны» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.explain: «хороших лошадях» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.

The expression on all faces showed the tension people feel at the approach of those in authority. The prisoners thronged together and were pushed off the road. The convoy formed up.

cases.sentence: — и только что проехали сытые конвойные, как прогремела карета цугом, на ___.
cases.explain: «серых лошадях» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “The Emperor! The Emperor! The Marshal! The Duke!” and hardly had the sleek cavalry passed, before a carriage drawn by six gray horses rattled by. Pierre caught a glimpse of a man in a three-cornered hat with a tranquil look on his handsome, plump, white face. It was one of the marshals. His eye fell on Pierre’s large and striking figure, and in the expression with which he frowned and looked away Pierre thought he detected sympathy and a desire to conceal that sympathy.

cases.sentence: Каратаев смотрел на Пьера своими добрыми ___, подернутыми теперь слезою и видимо подзывал его к себе, хотел сказать что-то.
cases.explain: «круглыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Karatáev looked at Pierre with his kindly round eyes now filled with tears, evidently wishing him to come near that he might say something to him. But Pierre was not sufficiently sure of himself. He made as if he did not notice that look and moved hastily away.

cases.sentence: Они оба были бледны и в выражении их лиц — один из них робко взглянул на Пьера — было что-то похожее на то, что он видел в ___ на казни.
cases.explain: «молодом солдате» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: From behind, where Karatáev had been sitting, came the sound of a shot. Pierre heard it plainly, but at that moment he remembered that he had not yet finished reckoning up how many stages still remained to Smolénsk—a calculation he had begun before the marshal went by. And he again started reckoning. Two French soldiers ran past Pierre, one of whom carried a lowered and smoking gun. They both looked pale, and in the expression on their faces—one of them glanced timidly at Pierre—there was something resembling what he had seen on the face of the young soldier at the execution. Pierre looked at the soldier and remembered that, two days before, that man had burned his shirt while drying it at the fire and how they had laughed at him.

cases.sentence: Пьер посмотрел на солдата и вспомнил о том, как этот солдат ___ сжег, высушивая на костре, свою рубаху и как смеялись над ним.
cases.explain: «третьего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: From behind, where Karatáev had been sitting, came the sound of a shot. Pierre heard it plainly, but at that moment he remembered that he had not yet finished reckoning up how many stages still remained to Smolénsk—a calculation he had begun before the marshal went by. And he again started reckoning. Two French soldiers ran past Pierre, one of whom carried a lowered and smoking gun. They both looked pale, and in the expression on their faces—one of them glanced timidly at Pierre—there was something resembling what he had seen on the face of the young soldier at the execution. Pierre looked at the soldier and remembered that, two days before, that man had burned his shirt while drying it at the fire and how they had laughed at him.

cases.sentence: «___, о чем она воет?» подумал Пьер.
cases.explain: «Экая дура» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Behind him, where Karatáev had been sitting, the dog began to howl. “What a stupid beast! Why is it howling?” thought Pierre.

cases.sentence: Солдаты товарищи, шедшие рядом с Пьером, не оглядывались так же, как и он на то место, с которого послышался выстрел и потом вой собаки; но ___ лежало на всех лицах.
cases.explain: «строгое выражение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: His comrades, the prisoner soldiers walking beside him, avoided looking back at the place where the shot had been fired and the dog was howling, just as Pierre did, but there was a set look on all their faces.
